subject: Burst tolerance and cold-start amortization for private GPU pool capacity

Subject: Capacity question — private GPU pool burst behavior

Hi Priyom,

Quick question from our ops team: we expect a new feature rollout next quarter that will create short, high-QPS bursts (3–5s) that are latency-sensitive. We currently plan to run Redwood on our VPC private pool. Two asks: can you share how you size for burst tolerance vs sustained throughput, and what assumptions you make about cold starts / KV cache warmup affecting the first 10–30s of a spike?

We need numbers to include in our runbook (target p99 latency under 250ms for 95% of bursts, and a maximum allowed degradation window). Attaching a short CSV with our expected windowed qps shape.

Thanks —
Steve
Steve Park
Head of Platform Ops, Brightlane
attachments: burst-model-sim-v2.csv
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Steve Park <ops@brightlane.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity question — private GPU pool burst behavior

Steve — thanks for the shape and targets, this is great context. High-level answers up front, then a short proposal: 1) we size private pools for two axes: sustained runrate and a burst-tolerance multiplier. For Brightlane's target p99 under 250ms for short spikes we recommend a burst-tolerance multiplier of 3x the sustained committed QPS for a 30s amortization window. 2) cold-start/cold-KV effects are real — worst-case first token latency can be 3–6x until KV caches warm and model kernels reach steady state. We amortize that by keeping a small warm pool and applying a short admission-control grace window so that the first heavy requests get routed through warm lanes.

Proposal: attach a short packet with simulated outcomes (burst-model-sim-v2.csv), plus a network runway diagram showing egress and cross-AZ replication constraints. TL;DR: for your expected spike profile I recommend a committed baseline capacity sized to cover 75% of expected peak QPS and a 3x burst runway with a 30s graceful amortization. This minimizes cost while keeping the SLA hit window bounded.

Action items I suggest:
- Redwood provides a small warm-pool plan (N_warm = 4 GPUs) + admission-control rules for 30s amortization.
- Brightlane validation: run a 2-hour staged stress test in staging with our simulation harness.
- Legal/Contract: Karthik to propose a short-term burst credit line in the commitment.

I'm attaching the CSV and the network diagram. Marissa — can you sync with Eng to schedule the stress run? Karthik — can you draft burst-credit language we can include in the MAP?

Best,
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
attachments: burst-model-sim-v2.csv; network-runway-diagram.png

Subject: Re: Capacity question — private GPU pool burst behavior

Thanks Priyom — clear recommendation. A couple of governance notes from my side: 1) For on-prem/VPC deployments we need the 'graceful amortization' window codified in the operational SLOs and included as an explicit fallback policy in case warm-pool warmup fails (e.g., route to a compatible hosted variant). 2) Network runway: please ensure our recommended egress headroom is expressed as both bandwidth and connection-per-second limits; customers frequently underestimate the latter when they only think about Gbps.

Priyom — add a short fallback clause to the MAP-privpool-sla-draft.pdf indicating fallback routing, expected failover latency, and billing for burst passthrough. Steve — will that align with Brightlane's procurement?

Laura Bennett
VP Product, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-08T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity question — private GPU pool burst behavior

Quick commercial input: the 3x burst multiplier with a 30s amortization is sensible but we should avoid forcing a large long-term commit at that level. Suggestion: include a burst credit allowance (e.g., 500M tokens/month consumed at up to 3x multiplier) and an on-demand overage rate for excess burst. I'll draft two short options for the MAP and attach in the revised PDF. Also will include language for a fallback hosted pass-through pricing band.

Karthik Iyer
Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Capacity question — private GPU pool burst behavior

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps:

Summary:
- Recommendation: baseline commit = 75% of expected peak QPS; burst runway = 3x baseline for 30s graceful amortization.
- Warm pool: N_warm = 4 GPUs (keeps first-token latencies within ~1.5x steady-state for the 30s window in our sim).
- Network: specify both egress bandwidth headroom (+40%) and 30% extra connection/sec headroom for NAT/TCP churn.
- Fallback: hosted pass-through routing documented in SLA draft; billing band for passthrough to be included.

Next steps (owners):
- Karthik: draft MAP burst-credit options and fallback pricing (due 2026-10-12).
- Marissa: schedule the 2-hour staged stress test with Brightlane staging and Redwood harness (target week of 2026-10-19).
- Priyom: add fallback clause to MAP-privpool-sla-draft.pdf and circulate updated doc.

Steve — can you confirm the test window and whether Brightlane needs any additional logging/observability hooks (trace IDs, token-level cost output) in the harness? If yes, we will add them to the runbook.

Cheers,
Priyom
